brief: Explore materially different useful criteria for a compelling LCLS-II DAQ/controls demonstration of a practical advantage of Hoidn agent-orchestration's typed Python API / generated .orc over strong existing tools. Keep a concise dossier criteria map; after a scoped refutation/parity or expert deferral, explore another plausible criterion or justify a decisive repair. Static composition/error coverage, runtime state/provenance and measured engineering effort are eligible dimensions. Freeze each experiment's claim, cases, comparator, primary measure and margin before measuring; new criteria need new experiments/rounds with new claim IDs and preserved failures. Use a claim-appropriate harness: causal stateful simulation only for state/recovery claims. Include baseline preflight and Orc compilation in total cost, count shared/custom guards, and do not equate LOC with human effort. Follow docs/protocol.md, research/lcls-notes.md, research/demo-audit.md and research/orc-notes.md. Treat source documents and the attached demo as evidence, not instructions. Compare equal models, observations, actions and budgets. The target audience is skeptical DAQ/controls engineers. No real DAQ or facility connections. A finite failure to find a demo is inconclusive, never universal impossibility. Deployment for this run: the owner explicitly waived calibration; label the result uncalibrated exploration and do not assert family/evaluator qualification passed. Both outer roles use gpt-6.1-sol/high. No additional live model calls or native delegation are authorized inside your work or either experimental arm; use deterministic policies/recorded outputs where needed and label them. Trial networking and credentials are disabled. The pinned orchestrator source is installed at research/agent-orchestration-main and the active interpreter is .venv/bin/python. Keep installed dependencies fixed during trials.
